card.title: Ondal, Lending & Personal Banking
card.subtitle: A mobile banking experience combining fast lending with everyday banking for underserved UK consumers.

hero.title: Ondal, Lending & Personal Banking
hero.summary: A mobile banking experience combining fast lending with everyday banking for underserved UK consumers.

blocks.html:
Ondal is a mobile banking and lending product for underserved UK consumers who need fast access to credit alongside everyday banking. Building on an existing payday lending business, Ondal expanded into personal banking to bring borrowing, repayments, accounts, cards, and payments into one experience.

Mid-project, a banking provider change required us to rethink payment and card flows, while the scope expanded to multiple currencies, accounts, and savings pots.

As Product Designer, I owned the end-to-end mobile experience across research, UX/UI design, prototyping, and validation. I designed key lending and banking journeys and worked closely with Engineering and Compliance to keep the experience simple, compliant, and technically feasible as the banking provider and product scope changed.

blocks.title: Business goals
items: Expand from payday lending into personal banking
Reduce friction across loan applications and repayments
Build trust with underserved banking customers
Deliver a compliant product ready for Beta

items.challenge: Limited access to traditional banking and reliance on high-friction short-term lending

items.goal: Access funds again with minimal effort

items.challenge: Unfamiliar with, or wary of, traditional banking processes

blocks.html:
Rather than treating lending and banking as separate products, I designed them as one connected customer journey.
We focused on two critical experiences:

- Helping a first-time borrower transition into banking with minimal additional setup.
- Making repeat borrowing faster for verified customers.

In-app onboarding and KYC were deferred to reduce implementation risk. At the same time, multi-currency accounts and savings pots were brought into the initial scope, so the underlying experience needed to support future complexity from the start.

items.finding: Returning borrowers repeatedly entered the same information when applying for another loan.
items.insight: Make repeat borrowing faster with pre-filled applications for verified customers.

items.finding: Repayment decisions often happened under financial stress.
The banking provider changed during development, altering available payment and card capabilities.
items.insight: Redesigned payment and card management around the new API constraints while keeping the customer experience consistent.

items.finding: The scope expanded to include multiple currencies, accounts, and savings pots.
items.insight: Created an information architecture that could support these products without significantly increasing navigation complexity.

blocks.html: Because Ondal had not yet launched publicly, the impact of the work was measured through design validation and Beta readiness rather than post-launch business metrics.

The biggest lesson was designing for change.
The banking provider migration and expanding product scope pushed me to think beyond individual screens and design a flexible system that could adapt to changing technical and business requirements.

It also reinforced the importance of treating lending and banking as one connected experience, rather than adding banking features onto an existing loan product.

The next step after Beta would be to measure real customer behaviour and use those findings to refine the experience after launch.
